reasons: Classification is correct: Article VIX provides the Licensed Technology wholly 'AS IS', disclaims all express and implied warranties and expressly negates any commitment that nonconformity to the Documentation will be corrected, with no conformance warranty or repair/replace/refund remedy anywhere — squarely the rule's walk-away scenario, so it fails even the 90-day fallback.

The redline is actionable and correctly targeted: it prefixes the disclaimer with an 'EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE' carve-out (preserving the rest of the disclaimer, i.e. minimal edit) and appends an express-warranty section with 12-month software conformance, workmanlike services, legal compliance, no malicious code, and a repair/replace/refund remedy — matching the preferred position and model language.

The inserted text opens with 'Notwithstanding the foregoing', which neutralizes the residual error-free / no-correction disclaimers in p0113–p0116 that would otherwise conflict with the new conformance warranty.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required tone and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the 90-day fallback as the playbook contemplates.

Minor drafting nit (does not affect the verdict): the insert uses 'Software', 'Specifications' and 'Technical Support Services' where the Agreement defines 'Licensed Software' / 'Licensed Technology' and may not define 'Specifications'; conforming the defined terms would tighten the edit.
